from IPython.display import HTML

<!-- ══════════════════════════════════════════════

════════════════════════════════════════════════ -->
<div class="ei-tabs">
  <button class="ei-tab-btn active" onclick="switchTab('overview', this)">Overview</button>
  <button class="ei-tab-btn" onclick="switchTab('report', this)">Report Analysis</button>
  <button class="ei-tab-btn" onclick="switchTab('individual', this)">Individual Scores</button>
  <button class="ei-tab-btn" onclick="switchTab('comparison', this)">AI Models Inter-Comparison</button>
  <button class="ei-tab-btn" onclick="switchTab('aivsnumeric', this)">AI vs Numeric System</button>
  <button class="ei-tab-btn" onclick="switchTab('infrastructure', this)">Infrastructure</button>
</div>

<!-- ══════════════════════════════════════════════
     TAB 1 — OVERVIEW
════════════════════════════════════════════════ -->
<div class="ei-tab-panel active" id="tab-overview">

  <p class="ei-intro">
    An LED bulb left on for an hour uses about 0.002 kWh. A one-hour video call emits around
    600 g of CO₂e. A one-hour car journey at 60 km/h can emit more than ten kilograms.
    These everyday activities all carry a measurable energy and carbon cost. Running a
    forecasting model is no different, the difference is that this cost happens inside a
    data center, out of sight, rather than in front of the user.
  </p>

  <p class="ei-intro">
    This is the purpose of the <strong>Energy Impact</strong> page: to measure and report,
    in a transparent way, the energy consumption and CO₂ emissions of the ocean forecasting
    models available on Oceanbench, both during training and during inference (the phase
    where a model is actually used to produce a forecast). A model's value should not be
    assessed on accuracy alone. Its energy footprint is equally relevant when deciding which
    model to use. Presenting both dimensions together is meant to support that decision.
  </p>

  <div class="ei-callout">
    <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">
      <circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"/><line x1="12" y1="8" x2="12" y2="12"/><line x1="12" y1="16" x2="12.01" y2="16"/>
    </svg>
    <div>
      Measurements use the
      <a href="https://github.com/mlco2/codecarbon" style="color: #1D4ED8;">codecarbon</a>
      open-source library for carbon tracking.
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="ei-section-title-overview ">Reference values</div>

  <p>
    Figures expressed in kWh or g of CO₂e are not always intuitive on their own. The
    reference values below provide a few familiar points of comparison, useful for putting
    the model figures presented later on this page into perspective.
  </p>

  <p class="ei-sublabel">Energy consumption in 1 hour</p>
  <div class="ei-ref-grid">
    <div class="ei-ref-card">
      <div class="ei-ref-card-label">Usage</div>
      <div class="ei-ref-card-item">LED bulb</div>
      <div class="ei-ref-card-value">0.002</div>
      <div class="ei-ref-card-unit">kWh</div>
    </div>
    <div class="ei-ref-card2">
      <div class="ei-ref-card-label">Usage</div>
      <div class="ei-ref-card-item">LED TV</div>
      <div class="ei-ref-card-value">0.10</div>
      <div class="ei-ref-card-unit">kWh</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <p class="ei-sublabel" style="margin-top: 1rem;">CO₂ emissions in 1 hour</p>
  <div class="ei-ref-grid">
    <div class="ei-ref-card">
      <div class="ei-ref-card-label">Usage</div>
      <div class="ei-ref-card-item">Video call streaming</div>
      <div class="ei-ref-card-value">600</div>
      <div class="ei-ref-card-unit">gCO₂e</div>
    </div>
    <div class="ei-ref-card2">
      <div class="ei-ref-card-label">Usage</div>
      <div class="ei-ref-card-item">Petrol car (60 km/h)</div>
      <div class="ei-ref-card-value">10200</div>
      <div class="ei-ref-card-unit">gCO₂e</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <p class="ei-sources">
    Sources:
    <a href="https://www.energybot.com/energy-usage/led-light-bulb.html">LED Bulb</a> ·
    <a href="https://www.nexamp.com/blog/do-tvs-use-a-lot-of-electricity">LED TV</a> ·
    <a href="https://medium.com/@zodhyatech/how-much-co2-do-you-emit-in-a-day-60be76e491dc">Video streaming &amp; car</a>
  </p>

  <div class="ei-section-title-overview ">Formulas</div>

  <p>
    These figures are derived from a consistent measurement method. While a model runs,
    codecarbon records the power drawn by the CPU, GPU and RAM. This value is then adjusted
    using the data center's efficiency (PUE) to obtain the total energy consumed. That energy
    is finally converted into a CO₂ figure using the carbon intensity of the local electricity
    mix. The two formulas below summarize this process.
  </p>
  <div class="ei-formulas-section ">
    <div class="ei-formula-block">
      <div class="ei-formula-row">
        <span class="ei-formula-label">Energy</span>
        <span>= (CPU<sub>consumption</sub> + GPU<sub>consumption</sub> + RAM<sub>consumption</sub>) × PUE</span>
      </div>
      <div class="ei-formula-row">
        <span class="ei-formula-label">Emissions</span>
        <span>= Energy<sub>consumption</sub> × Coef<sub>energymix</sub></span>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="ei-callout">
    <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">
      <circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"/><line x1="12" y1="8" x2="12" y2="12"/><line x1="12" y1="16" x2="12.01" y2="16"/>
    </svg>
    <div><strong>PUE</strong> — Power Usage Effectiveness: ratio of total data center energy to IT equipment energy.</div>
  </div>

  <div class="ei-section-title-overview "> System list presentation</div>

  <p>
    The list below presents the ocean forecasting models covered by this page, including
    both AI-based models and a physics-based numerical model. Each of them is measured using
    the method described above, allowing their energy and carbon footprints to be compared
    on a consistent basis.
  </p>

<div class="ei-models-list">

  <div class="ei-model-row-card">
    <div class="ei-model-row-accent" style="background:#D9583E;"></div>
    <div class="ei-model-row-name">GLO12</div>
    <div class="ei-model-row-provider">Provider · Mercator Ocean International</div>
    <div class="ei-model-row-desc">GLO12 is Mercator Ocean's operational physics-based global ocean forecasting system, combining governing physical equations with observational data assimilation at 1/12° high resolution to deliver dynamically consistent forecasts of temperature, salinity, currents, and sea surface height.</div>
  </div>

  <div class="ei-model-row-card">
    <div class="ei-model-row-accent" style="background:#378ADD;"></div>
    <div class="ei-model-row-name">GLONET</div>
    <div class="ei-model-row-provider">Provider · Mercator Ocean International</div>
    <div class="ei-model-row-desc">GLONET is a neural-operator-based global ocean forecasting model emphasizing physical consistency and mesoscale dynamics preservation rather than only minimizing statistical forecast errors.</div>
  </div>

  <div class="ei-model-row-card">
    <div class="ei-model-row-accent" style="background:#4A3E8C;"></div>
    <div class="ei-model-row-name">GLONET2</div>
    <div class="ei-model-row-provider">Provider · Mercator Ocean International</div>
    <div class="ei-model-row-desc">GLONET2 is a neural-operator-based global ocean forecasting model emphasizing physical consistency and mesoscale dynamics preservation rather than only minimizing statistical forecast errors.</div>
  </div>

  <div class="ei-model-row-card">
    <div class="ei-model-row-accent" style="background:#1D9E75;"></div>
    <div class="ei-model-row-name">WenHai</div>
    <div class="ei-model-row-provider">Provider · Ocean Univ. China, Laoshan Lab., Univ. of Science and Technology of China, MOI</div>
    <div class="ei-model-row-desc">WenHai is a transformer-based global ocean forecasting model designed to incorporate both ocean dynamics and atmospheric forcing.</div>
  </div>

  <div class="ei-model-row-card">
    <div class="ei-model-row-accent" style="background:#D4537E;"></div>
    <div class="ei-model-row-name">XiHe</div>
    <div class="ei-model-row-provider">Provider · National Univ. of Defense Technology, Central South Univ., China Univ. of Petroleum (East China), Tianjin Univ. of Science and Technology, Fudan Univ., National Marine Environmental Forecasting Center, MOI</div>
    <div class="ei-model-row-desc">XiHe is a hierarchical transformer ocean forecasting model optimized for very fast and stable predictions at global eddy-resolving scale. Instead of recursive forecasting, the model predicts each lead time independently to reduce error accumulation.</div>
  </div>

  <div class="ei-model-row-card">
    <div class="ei-model-row-accent" style="background:#D4C853;"></div>
    <div class="ei-model-row-name">LangYa</div>
    <div class="ei-model-row-provider">Provider · Inst. of Oceanology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Key Laboratory of Ocean Observation and Forecasting, Key Laboratory of Ocean Circulation and Waves, MOI</div>
    <div class="ei-model-row-desc">LangYa is a cross-spatiotemporal transformer model that explicitly incorporates atmosphere-ocean coupling and adaptive thermocline-aware learning.</div>
  </div>

</div>


</div><!-- /tab-overview -->

════════════════════════════════════════════════ -->
<div class="ei-tab-panel" id="tab-individual">

  <!-- GLO12 -->
  <div class="ei-section-title">GLO12</div>
  <div class="ei-callout">
    <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">
      <circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"/><line x1="12" y1="8" x2="12" y2="12"/><line x1="12" y1="16" x2="12.01" y2="16"/>
    </svg>
    <div><strong>Note:</strong> The result value depends a lot on the infrastructure and resources used by the code. To see the test specifications, go to the Infrastructure tab.</div>
  </div>
  <p style="font-size: 13.5px; color: #666; margin-bottom: 1rem;">
    Results are based on average 9 runs. Measurements taken on the Météo-France (Belenos) supercomputer in Toulouse.
    The ± margin corresponds to a 95% confidence interval based on Student's t-distribution.
  </p>
  <div class="ei-model-card">
    <div class="ei-model-card-header">
      <span class="ei-model-badge">Run</span>
    </div>
    <table class="ei-table">
      <thead><tr><th>Metric</th><th>Value</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>Energy (kWh)</td><td><span class="ei-result">18.4 (± 1.92)</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td>CO₂ emissions (gCO₂e)</td><td><span class="ei-result">883 (± 91.9)</span></td></tr>
        <tr><td>Duration (seconds)</td><td><span class="ei-result">2843</span></td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>

  <!-- Glonet -->
  <div class="ei-section-title">GLONET</div>
  <p style="font-size: 13.5px; color: #666; margin-bottom: 1rem;">
    Results are based on average 10 runs. Measurements taken on Datalab EDITO.
    The ± margin corresponds to a 95% confidence interval based on Student's t-distribution.
  </p>
  <div class="ei-model-card">
    <div class="ei-model-card-header">
      <span class="ei-model-badge">Inference Process</span>
    </div>
    <table class="ei-table">
      <thead><tr><th>Metric</th><th>Value</th></tr></thead>

<!-- ══════════════════════════════════════════════
     TAB 3 — REPORT ANALTSIS
════════════════════════════════════════════════ -->
<div class="ei-tab-panel" id="tab-report">
  <p class="ei-intro">
    This report synthesizes the key results from the other tabs into several evidence-backed findings: what
    actually drives energy consumption during inference, where the numbers can and cannot be compared, and
    what that means in practice for how models and infrastructure should be chosen. Each finding is
    illustrated with the same charts shown in AI models Comparaison Charts section, reused as-is, not redrawn, so
    every conclusion can be traced straight back to its source.
  </p>

  <h2 class="ei-title">
    Measurement methodology across infrastructures
  </h2>
  <p class="ei-report">
    Results are not captured the same way everywhere, which matters when comparing infrastructures. On Destination Earth Data Lake (Eumetsat) and Lir, everything is measured with Codecarbon, which runs at full capability there: CPU energy uses the auto-detected TDP together with % usage and duration, GPU energy comes from pyNVML, which reports exact consumption at a given time that is then multiplied across each measured interval, and RAM energy is estimated by approximating the number of memory modules from total RAM size.
    On Datalab EDITO, security and user restrictions prevent Codecarbon from running at full capability. CPU energy still goes through Codecarbon, but the CPU TDP has to be entered manually since it can't be auto-detected there. GPU energy can't rely on pyNVML at all, so it's estimated the same way as CPU: TDP is read from nvidia-smi, and energy is computed by sampling % GPU usage at fixed intervals and multiplying by TDP and elapsed time. RAM measurement is unaffected and still goes through Codecarbon normally.
    This sampling-based estimation is itself a coarser approximation than pyNVML's direct readings, and the same non-linearity between usage and power draw noted for GPUs likely affects CPU TDP-based estimates too, adding another layer of uncertainty on top of the interval sampling itself.
    Because of these differences, absolute energy values shouldn't be compared directly across infrastructures, one method is simply less accurate than the other. Comparisons remain meaningful within a single infrastructure, where all models are captured with the same method.
  </p> 

  <h2 class="ei-title">
    Infrastructure impact
  </h2>
    <p>Even without cross-infrastructure comparisons, some lessons still hold within each one. A more economical GPU, like the one used on Datalab EDITO, tends to consume less energy overall than a stronger GPU such as those on Lir or Eumetsat. For most of a run, GPU usage sits near 0%, but the card stays on and keeps drawing power regardless, so a less powerful GPU can end up being the more energy-efficient choice precisely because it isn't idling at as high a baseline draw.
    
    <p class="ei-sublabel">GPU idle</p>
    <div class="ei-ref-grid2">
      <div class="ei-ref-card">
        <div class="ei-ref-card-label">Destination Earth Data Lake (Eumetsat)</div>
        <div class="ei-ref-card-item">NVIDIA H100 (80 GB HBM2e)</div>
        <div class="ei-ref-card-value">50 W</div>
      </div>
      <div class="ei-ref-card">
        <div class="ei-ref-card-label">Lir</div>
        <div class="ei-ref-card-item">NVIDIA H100 (80 GB HBM3)</div>
        <div class="ei-ref-card-value">68 W</div>
      </div>
      <div class="ei-ref-card2">
        <div class="ei-ref-card-label">Datalab EDITO</div>
        <div class="ei-ref-card-item">NVIDIA RTX A6000 (48 GB)</div>
        <div class="ei-ref-card-value">35 W</div>
      </div>
    </div>

    The same logic applies to CPUs: Eumetsat uses more CPU than Lir for the same GPU, and consumes more energy per inference as a result, since the extra CPU capacity sits mostly idle during inference without saving any time. That said, more CPU isn't always wasted, GLONET and GLONET2 both have a pre-inference phase that runs faster with more CPU available, so the right amount of CPU depends on which phase of the pipeline is being optimized, not on a blanket rule.
  </p> 


  <h2 class="ei-title">
    Number of operations and energy consumption
  </h2>
  <p class="ei-report">
    There is a clear linear correlation between the number of operations and energy consumption, with a Pearson coefficient of 0.95 on Lir, 0.95 on Datalab EDITO, and 0.87 on Eumetsat. These operations are computed by the GPU during inference, so the relationship is naturally bounded by GPU efficiency.
    <div style="padding:1rem 0; margin-top:1.5rem;">
    <p style="font-size:13px; color:#888; margin:0 0 1rem;">Correlation — inference energy vs. number of operations during inference</p>
    <div style="position:relative; width:100%; height:320px;">
      <canvas id="correlationChart2"></canvas>
    </div>
  </div>

    Some models still deviate from this trend, GLONET2 in particular consumes more than its operation count alone would predict. This is likely explained by a higher average GPU usage during inference with no low peaks, which can make the run take longer overall despite the workload itself being similar, since the relationship between GPU energy draw and % usage is not linear. Measurement uncertainty can also play a role: two models with a similar operation count may show slightly different consumption even across repeated runs, and these small gaps shouldn't be over-interpreted as meaningful differences unless they clearly exceed run-to-run variability.
  </p>
  


  <h2 class="ei-title">
    Duration and consumption
  </h2>
    As expected, there is a clear correlation between the duration and the energy consumption with hight pearson coefficient. In fact more time a program use resource more energy he will consume regardless the intensity of the usage. During inference the GPU usage dominate, then it’s more how many time you use it that will define your energy consumed than the intensity of the usage, since the energy you consume is not evloving linearly with the usage intensity.

  </p>
  
  <div style="padding:1rem 0; margin-top:1.5rem;">
    <p style="font-size:13px; color:#888; margin:0 0 1rem;">Correlation — full inference process duration vs. number of energy consumed during full process</p>
    <div style="position:relative; width:100%; height:320px;">
      <canvas id="correlationDurationOpsChart2"></canvas>
    </div>
  </div>

    <div style="padding:1rem 0; margin-top:1.5rem;">
    <p style="font-size:13px; color:#888; margin:0 0 1rem;">Correlation — inference duration vs. energy consumed during inference</p>
    <div style="position:relative; width:100%; height:320px;">
      <canvas id="correlationDurationEnergyChart2"></canvas>
    </div>
  </div>


  <h2 class="ei-title">
    Data fetching: local vs. S3 !!TO BE CHANGE!!
  </h2>
  <p class="ei-report">
    The original pipeline (for GLONET only) fetched data from Copernicus Marine, wrote it to a temporary file, uploaded it to an S3 bucket, and then re-downloaded it from there during inference. The local variant fetches the same data directly into a local folder and passes local file paths at inference time, skipping the S3 round trip entirely for files that are only ever used within the same job.
    This local method is faster (61s vs 75s, about 19% less) and uses roughly 10% less power. The result makes sense: the original approach sends data away and brings it back down again for no real benefit, since the files never leave the job. Removing that extra upload-then-download step cuts both transfer time and the associated energy draw. It's similar to streaming vs. downloading a movie: streaming keeps you dependent on the network for the whole playback, with the latency and instability that implies, while downloading first means only the initial fetch depends on the connection, everything after that is local and unaffected by network conditions, as long as you have the storage for it.
  </p>

  <h2 class="ei-title">
    Number of parameters: no clear impact
  </h2>
  <p class="ei-report">
    There is no clear correlation between a model's number of parameters and its energy consumption during inference. This makes sense once you consider that energy use depends more on what is done with the parameters than on how many there are. Note that parameter count can still be a reasonable proxy for accuracy, it just isn't one for energy efficiency, and the two shouldn't be conflated. Xihe and WenHai illustrate this well: their parameter counts are close (9% apart), yet their energy consumption differs by 25% to 50% depending on the infrastructure.
  </p>
  <div style="padding:1rem 0; margin-top:1.5rem;">
    <p style="font-size:13px; color:#888; margin:0 0 1rem;">Model size — number of parameters used by each AI model </p>
    <div style="position:relative; width:100%; height:260px;">
      <canvas id="nbParamsChart2"></canvas>
    </div>
  </div>


  <h2 class="ei-title">
    GLONET vs. GLONET2
  </h2>
    Although their names are similar, GLONET and GLONET2 differ in several key aspects. First, GLONET is based on three models that make predictions at different levels. Therefore, generating a single prediction requires running all three models and merging their outputs into the final prediction, whereas GLONET2 relies on a single model. Second, GLONET2 uses significantly fewer parameters than GLONET (80M vs. 417M). Third, although GLONET2 performs slightly more operations during inference than GLONET, but all these operations are executed within a single model rather than across three separate models. As result, GLONET2 is faster and consumes less energy than GLONET, which is consistent with the observed correlation between inference time and energy consumption.
  </p>

  <h2 class="ei-title">
    Inference vs. Inference process
  </h2>

  <p class="ei-report">
    On this Energy Impact page, we discuss two different things: first, the Inference, which refers to the prediction/forecast of our model over 10 or 7 days. Second, there is the Inference process, which refers to three phases: the first is the pre-inference phase, where we download the model we are going to use and fetch the data needed to run the inference. The second is the inference phase presented above. The third phase is the post-inference phase, which relates to saving and uploading the inference results. Each phase consumes a different amount of energy.
  </p>
    <div style="padding: 1rem 0;">
      <div style="font-size: 15px; font-weight: 500; color: #111; margin-bottom: 12px;">Energy consumed part — GLONET2 Inference Process</div>
      <div id="stacked-bar-glonet22" style="display: flex; width: 100%; height: 80px; border-radius: 8px; overflow: hidden;"></div>
      <div id="bar-legend-glonet22" style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 12px; margin-top: 14px; font-size: 12px; color: #888;"></div>
    </div>

  <p class="ei-report">
    The energy consumed during each phase is highly correlated with the duration of the phase, but not only that, in fact the inference phase represents a higher percentage of energy consumption than of time, which is explained by the fact that it is the phase that uses the GPU intensively, whereas the GPU is idle during the other two phases.
  </p>

    <div style="padding: 1rem 0;">
      <div style="font-size: 15px; font-weight: 500; color: #111; margin-bottom: 12px;">Duration part — GLONET2 Inference Process</div>
      <div id="stacked-bar-glonet2_part22" style="display: flex; width: 100%; height: 20px; border-radius: 8px; overflow: hidden;"></div>
      <div id="bar-legend-glonet2_part22" style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 12px; margin-top: 14px; font-size: 12px; color: #888;"></div>
    </div>

  <p class="ei-report">
    Finally, both approaches (Inference and Inference Process) to evaluating our model's consumption are relevant, since they represent two different things: one focuses on the model itself, the other on the entire workflow required to obtain our prediction using the model.
  </p>


 <h2 class="ei-title">
    Conclusions and Guidelines
  </h2>

  <p class="ei-report">
    <strong>What can we learn from this study.</strong> Taken together, these results tell a fairly clear story. The first lesson is that AI models can have very different energy footprints even when they serve a similar purpose: WenHai, for instance, consumes 5-8 times more energy than GLONET2. This alone shows that energy consumption cannot be assumed from a model's role or reputation, it has to be measured.
    Infrastructure adds another layer to this picture: hardware, available CPU capacity, and network conditions all shift the numbers, which is why the same model can score differently depending on where it runs, and why absolute values are only meaningful when compared within a single infrastructure (see "Measurement methodology").
    Underneath these variations, some consistent patterns emerge: energy consumption is closely tied to factors like run duration and the number of operations performed, which makes them reliable signals for anticipating a model's impact.
    And this isn't only about the model itself, how data is handled around it matters too: keeping files local and avoiding unnecessary round trips to remote storage reduces both time and energy at once (see "Data fetching: local vs. S3").
  </p>

  <p class="ei-report">
    <strong>How can we improve our footprint.</strong> These lessons translate into a few concrete levers. The first, and probably the simplest, is choosing infrastructure carefully, especially the GPU: two cards with similar computational performance can draw very different amounts of power, particularly at idle. Comparing GPU benchmarks and technical specs before committing to a setup, whether for inference or training, helps avoid paying an energy cost for performance that ends up unused.
    Beyond hardware, the models themselves can be optimized: reducing the number of operations (FLOPs) required for a prediction (see <a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.16070">OceanLight study</a>), for example through more efficient architectures, has a direct effect on consumption. .
    A third lever sits at the data layer: avoiding or limiting dependencies on remote servers and buckets, whether for reading or writing, cuts down on both latency and the energy spent on transfers.
  </p>

</div>

require(['chartjs'], function(ChartModule) {

      { name:'XiHe',   mu:68.6,  ci:4.94, color:'#D4537E', fill:'212,83,126',  dash:[2,4] },
      { name:'LangYa', mu:14.74, ci:0.916, color:'#D4C853', fill:'212,200,83',  dash:[2,4] }
    ]
  };

  const STAGES     = ["pre-inference","inference","post-inference"];
  const BAR_COLORS = ["#96D3E2","#036aa1","#1C3A6E"];

  const ALL_BREAKDOWN = {
    A: [
      { name:'GLONET', values:[86.3,3.0,8.6] },
      { name:'GLONET2', values:[72.0,6.0,22.0]},

    ],
    B: [
      { name:'GLONET', values:[40.8,37.2,21.95] },
      { name:'GLONET2', values:[38.9,47.2,13.9] },
      { name:'WenHai', values:[20.68,66.1,13.2] },
      { name:'XiHe',   values:[24.0,56.0,20.0] },
      { name:'LangYa', values:[39.39,19.2,36.7] }
    ],
    C: [
      { name:'GLONET', values:[73.6,16.5,9.90] },
      { name:'GLONET2', values:[76.4,10.2,13.4] },
      { name:'WenHai', values:[32.5,36.3,31.2]},
      { name:'XiHe',   values:[28.9,31.4,39.7] },
      { name:'LangYa', values:[29.4,12.0,58.6] }
    ]
  };

  const ALL_INFERENCE  = { A:[6.20,1.16,19.4,9.10,0.521], B:[4.96,1.70,15.54,8.98,0.836], C:[7.50,1.31,27.3,21.2,1.77] };
  const ALL_NB_PARAMS  = { A:[417,80.3,125,117,8.57],  B:[417,80.3,125,117,8.57],  C:[417,80.3,125,117,8.57] };
  const ALL_NB_OPE     = { A:[76.5,100,469,173,6.21],    B:[76.5,100,469,173,6.21],    C:[76.5,100,469,173,6.21] };
  const MODEL_NAMES    = ['GLONET','GLONET2','WenHai','XiHe','LangYa'];
  const MODEL_COLORS   = ['#378ADD','#4A3E8C','#1D9E75','#D4537E','#D4C853'];

  // ── Duration data (seconds) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  const ALL_DURATION_TOTAL = {
    A: [2047, 275, 781, 648, 328],
    B: [447, 85, 868, 675, 180],
    C: [590, 176, 897, 967, 140]
  };
  const ALL_DURATION_INFERENCE = {
    A: [61, 11, 253, 117, 9.8],
    B: [112, 17, 440, 205, 22],
    C: [80, 12, 307, 247, 21]
  };
  // Plain energy array (Wh) mirroring ALL_MODELS.mu, reused for correlation charts.
  const ALL_ENERGY_TOTAL = {
    A: [134,  18.9, 49.7, 41.2, 20.9],
    B: [14.1, 3.1, 24.5, 17.3, 4.35],
    C: [45.5, 12.8, 75.1, 68.6, 14.74]
  };

  const ALL_ENERGY_INFERENCE = {
    A: [6.20, 1.16, 19.4, 9.10, 0.52],
    B: [4.96, 1.70, 15.54, 8.98, 0.84],
    C: [7.50, 1.31, 27.30, 21.20, 1.77]
  };

  let currentMachine  = 'B';
  let activeModels    = { GLONET:true, GLONET2:true, WenHai:true, XiHe:true, LangYa:true };

  // ── Helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  function activeIndices() {
    return MODEL_NAMES.map(function(_,i){ return i; })
                      .filter(function(i){ return activeModels[MODEL_NAMES[i]]; });
  }

  function filteredLabels() {
    return activeIndices().map(function(i){ return MODEL_NAMES[i]; });
  }

  // ── Chart 1 (line) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  function buildLineDatasets(machine) {
    var datasets = [];
    ALL_MODELS[machine].forEach(function(m) {
      if (!activeModels[m.name]) return;
      datasets.push({ label:m.name+' upper', data:runs.map(function(r){ return r*(m.mu+m.ci); }), borderColor:'rgba(0,0,0,0)', backgroundColor:'rgba('+m.fill+',0.22)', pointRadius:0, fill:false });
      datasets.push({ label:m.name+' lower', data:runs.map(function(r){ return r*(m.mu-m.ci); }), borderColor:'rgba(0,0,0,0)', backgroundColor:'rgba('+m.fill+',0.22)', pointRadius:0, fill:'-1' });
      datasets.push({ label:m.name, data:runs.map(function(r){ return r*m.mu; }), borderColor:m.color, backgroundColor:'transparent', borderWidth:2.5, borderDash:m.dash, pointRadius:3, pointBackgroundColor:m.color, tension:0.3 });
    });
    return datasets;
  }

  function buildLegend(machine) {
    var legend = document.getElementById('legend-container');
    if (!legend) return;
    legend.innerHTML = '';
    ALL_MODELS[machine].forEach(function(m) {
      if (!activeModels[m.name]) return;
      legend.innerHTML += '<span style="display:flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;">'
        +'<span style="width:20px;height:3px;background:'+m.color+';display:inline-block;border-radius:2px;"></span>'
        +'<span style="width:10px;height:10px;border-radius:2px;background:rgba('+m.fill+',0.30);display:inline-block;"></span>'
        +m.name+' — '+m.mu+' Wh/run (±'+m.ci+')'
        +'</span>';
    });
  }

  var lineChart = new Chart(document.getElementById('energyCompChart'), {
    type:'line',
    data:{ labels:runs, datasets:buildLineDatasets('B') },
    options:{
      responsive:true, maintainAspectRatio:false,
      animation:{ duration:500, easing:'easeInOutQuart' },
      interaction:{ mode:'index', intersect:false },
      plugins:{
        legend:{ display:false },
        tooltip:{
          filter:function(item){ return !item.dataset.label.includes('upper')&&!item.dataset.label.includes('lower'); },
          callbacks:{
            title:function(ctx){ return ctx[0].label+' run'+(ctx[0].label>1?'s':''); },
            label:function(ctx){

              var visModels = ALL_MODELS[currentMachine].filter(function(m){ return activeModels[m.name]; });
              var m = visModels[visIdx];
              if (!m) return '';
              var r = ctx.dataIndex;
              return ' '+m.name+': '+ctx.parsed.y.toFixed(1)+' Wh ['+(r*(m.mu-m.ci)).toFixed(1)+' – '+(r*(m.mu+m.ci)).toFixed(1)+']';
            }

  function buildBreakdownBars() {
    var container = document.getElementById('breakdown-container');

    container.innerHTML = '';
    ALL_BREAKDOWN['A'].forEach(function(model, mi) {
      var row = document.createElement('div');
      row.id = 'breakdown-row-'+mi;
      row.style.cssText = 'display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;';
      var label = document.createElement('div');
      label.style.cssText = 'width:64px;font-size:13px;font-weight:500;color:#111;flex-shrink:0;text-align:right;';

      var bar = document.createElement('div');
      bar.style.cssText = 'display:flex;flex:1;height:36px;border-radius:6px;overflow:hidden;';
      BAR_COLORS.forEach(function(color, i) {
        var seg = document.createElement('div');
        seg.id = 'seg-'+mi+'-'+i;
        seg.style.cssText = 'width:0%;background:'+color+';height:100%;transition:width 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1);cursor:default;';
        seg.onmouseenter = function(){ this.style.opacity='0.7'; };
        seg.onmouseleave = function(){ this.style.opacity='1'; };
        bar.appendChild(seg);
      });
      row.appendChild(bar);
      container.appendChild(row);
    });
    var legend = document.getElementById('breakdown-legend');
    if (legend && legend.innerHTML === '') {
      STAGES.forEach(function(stage, i) {
        legend.innerHTML += '<span style="display:flex;align-items:center;gap:5px;">'
          +'<span style="width:10px;height:10px;border-radius:2px;background:'+BAR_COLORS[i]+';flex-shrink:0;display:inline-block;"></span>'
          +stage+'</span>';
      });
    }
  }

      var total = model.values.reduce(function(a,b){ return a+b; },0);
      model.values.forEach(function(val, i) {

        if (seg) { seg.style.width=pct+'%'; seg.title=STAGES[i]+': '+val+' %'; }
      });
    });

  // ── Regression helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
  function linearRegression(pts) {
    var n=pts.length, sumX=0, sumY=0, sumXY=0, sumX2=0;
    pts.forEach(function(p){ sumX+=p.x; sumY+=p.y; sumXY+=p.x*p.y; sumX2+=p.x*p.x; });
    var slope=(n*sumXY-sumX*sumY)/(n*sumX2-sumX*sumX);
    var intercept=(sumY-slope*sumX)/n;
    return { slope:slope, intercept:intercept };
  }
  function linearRegressionThroughOrigin(pts) {
    var sumXY=0, sumX2=0;
    pts.forEach(function(p){ sumXY+=p.x*p.y; sumX2+=p.x*p.x; });
    var slope = sumX2===0 ? 0 : sumXY/sumX2;
    return { slope:slope, intercept:0 };
  }

  function pearson(pts) {
    var n=pts.length;
    var mx=pts.reduce(function(s,p){ return s+p.x; },0)/n;
    var my=pts.reduce(function(s,p){ return s+p.y; },0)/n;
    var num=pts.reduce(function(s,p){ return s+(p.x-mx)*(p.y-my); },0);
    var dx=Math.sqrt(pts.reduce(function(s,p){ return s+(p.x-mx)*(p.x-mx); },0));
    var dy=Math.sqrt(pts.reduce(function(s,p){ return s+(p.y-my)*(p.y-my); },0));
    return num/(dx*dy);
  }

  function buildCorrelationDatasets(machine) {
    var idx = activeIndices();
    var inferenceVals = idx.map(function(i){ return ALL_INFERENCE[machine][i]; });
    var opeVals       = idx.map(function(i){ return ALL_NB_OPE[machine][i]; });
    var scatterDatasets = idx.map(function(i, j) {
      return { type:'scatter', label:MODEL_NAMES[i], data:[{ x:inferenceVals[j], y:opeVals[j] }], backgroundColor:MODEL_COLORS[i], borderColor:MODEL_COLORS[i], pointRadius:10, pointHoverRadius:30, order:1 };
    });
    if (idx.length < 2) return { datasets:scatterDatasets, r:NaN };
    var pts = idx.map(function(i,j){ return { x:inferenceVals[j], y:opeVals[j] }; });
    var reg = linearRegressionThroughOrigin(pts);
    var r   = pearson(pts);
    var xMax = Math.max.apply(null,inferenceVals);
    var lineDataset = { type:'line', label:'Linear fit (r='+r.toFixed(2)+')', data:[{ x:0, y:0 },{ x:xMax*1.10, y:reg.slope*xMax*1.10 }], borderColor:'rgba(120,120,120,0.55)', borderWidth:1.5, borderDash:[5,4], pointRadius:0, fill:false, order:2 };
    return { datasets:scatterDatasets.concat([lineDataset]), r:r };
  }

  // ── Generic correlation builder (reused for duration-based charts) ───────
  function buildGenericCorrelationDatasets(machine, xData, yData) {
    var idx = activeIndices();
    var xVals = idx.map(function(i){ return xData[machine][i]; });
    var yVals = idx.map(function(i){ return yData[machine][i]; });
    var scatterDatasets = idx.map(function(i, j) {
      return { type:'scatter', label:MODEL_NAMES[i], data:[{ x:xVals[j], y:yVals[j] }], backgroundColor:MODEL_COLORS[i], borderColor:MODEL_COLORS[i], pointRadius:10, pointHoverRadius:30, order:1 };
    });
    if (idx.length < 2) return { datasets:scatterDatasets, r:NaN };
    var pts = idx.map(function(i,j){ return { x:xVals[j], y:yVals[j] }; });
    var reg = linearRegressionThroughOrigin(pts);
    var r   = pearson(pts);
    var xMax = Math.max.apply(null,xVals);
    var lineDataset = { type:'line', label:'Linear fit (r='+r.toFixed(2)+')', data:[{ x:0, y:0 },{ x:xMax*1.10, y:reg.slope*xMax*1.10 }], borderColor:'rgba(120,120,120,0.55)', borderWidth:1.5, borderDash:[5,4], pointRadius:0, fill:false, order:2 };
    return { datasets:scatterDatasets.concat([lineDataset]), r:r };
  }

  function pearsonForMachine(machine, xData, yData) {
    var idx = activeIndices();
    if (idx.length < 2) return NaN;
    var pts = idx.map(function(i){ return { x:xData[machine][i], y:yData[machine][i] }; });
    return pearson(pts);
  }

      id:'rLabelDurationOps',
      afterDraw:function(chart) {
        var r2 = pearsonForMachine(currentMachine, ALL_DURATION_TOTAL, ALL_ENERGY_TOTAL);
        if (isNaN(r2)) return;
        var ctx2 = chart.ctx;
        ctx2.save();
        ctx2.font='12px sans-serif'; ctx2.fillStyle='#aaa'; ctx2.textAlign='right';
        ctx2.fillText('Pearson r = '+r2.toFixed(2), chart.chartArea.right, chart.chartArea.top+16);
        ctx2.restore();
      }
    }]
  });

  // ── Chart 6ter (correlation duration vs energy consumed) ─────────────────
  var corrDurationEnergyInit = buildGenericCorrelationDatasets('B', ALL_DURATION_INFERENCE, ALL_ENERGY_INFERENCE);
  var correlationDurationEnergyChart = new Chart(document.getElementById('correlationDurationEnergyChart'), {
    type:'scatter',
    data:{ datasets:corrDurationEnergyInit.datasets },
    options:{
      responsive:true, maintainAspectRatio:false,
      animation:{ duration:500, easing:'easeInOutQuart' },

        legend:{ display:true, position:'bottom', labels:{ color:'#888', font:{size:11}, boxWidth:10, padding:14, filter:function(item){ return !item.text.startsWith('Linear'); } } },
        tooltip:{ callbacks:{ label:function(ctx){ if(ctx.dataset.type==='line') return null; return ' '+ctx.dataset.label+'  —  Duration: '+ctx.parsed.x.toFixed(0)+' s | Energy: '+ctx.parsed.y.toFixed(1)+' Wh'; } } }
      },
      scales:{
        x:{ title:{display:true,text:'Total process duration (s)',color:'#888',font:{size:12}}, ticks:{color:'#888',callback:function(v){ return v+' s'; }}, grid:{color:'rgba(128,128,128,0.08)'} },
        y:{ title:{display:true,text:'Energy consumed (Wh)',color:'#888',font:{size:12}}, ticks:{color:'#888',callback:function(v){ return v+' Wh'; }}, grid:{color:'rgba(128,128,128,0.08)'} }
      }
    },
    plugins:[{
      id:'rLabelDurationEnergy',

        ctx2.restore();
      }
    }]
  });

  var correlationDurationEnergyChart2 = new Chart(document.getElementById('correlationDurationEnergyChart2'), {
    type:'scatter',
    data:{ datasets:corrDurationEnergyInit.datasets },
    options:{
      responsive:true, maintainAspectRatio:false,
      animation:{ duration:500, easing:'easeInOutQuart' },

        legend:{ display:true, position:'bottom', labels:{ color:'#888', font:{size:11}, boxWidth:10, padding:14, filter:function(item){ return !item.text.startsWith('Linear'); } } },
        tooltip:{ callbacks:{ label:function(ctx){ if(ctx.dataset.type==='line') return null; return ' '+ctx.dataset.label+'  —  Duration: '+ctx.parsed.x.toFixed(0)+' s | Energy: '+ctx.parsed.y.toFixed(1)+' Wh'; } } }
      },
      scales:{
        x:{ title:{display:true,text:'Total process duration (s)',color:'#888',font:{size:12}}, ticks:{color:'#888',callback:function(v){ return v+' s'; }}, grid:{color:'rgba(128,128,128,0.08)'} },
        y:{ title:{display:true,text:'Energy consumed (Wh)',color:'#888',font:{size:12}}, ticks:{color:'#888',callback:function(v){ return v+' Wh'; }}, grid:{color:'rgba(128,128,128,0.08)'} }
      }
    },
    plugins:[{
      id:'rLabelDurationEnergy',
      afterDraw:function(chart) {
        var r2 = pearsonForMachine(currentMachine, ALL_DURATION_INFERENCE, ALL_ENERGY_INFERENCE);
        if (isNaN(r2)) return;
        var ctx2 = chart.ctx;
        ctx2.save();
        ctx2.font='12px sans-serif'; ctx2.fillStyle='#aaa'; ctx2.textAlign='right';
        ctx2.fillText('Pearson r = '+r2.toFixed(2), chart.chartArea.right, chart.chartArea.top+16);
        ctx2.restore();
      }
    }]
  });

  // ── Chart 7 (Option B — paired bars with % gap vs. reference) ────────────
  const INFRA_LABELS = { A:'Lir', B:'Datalab EDITO', C:'Eumetsat' };
  const INFRA_ORDER  = ['A','B','C'];
  let infraCompModelIndex = 0; // default: GLONET
  let infraCompRef        = 'B'; // default reference: Datalab EDITO

  function getInfraCompData() {
    var totals = INFRA_ORDER.map(function(m) {
      var model = ALL_MODELS[m].find(function(x){ return x.name === MODEL_NAMES[infraCompModelIndex]; });
      return model ? model.mu : 0;
    });
    var infs = INFRA_ORDER.map(function(m) { return ALL_INFERENCE[m][infraCompModelIndex]; });
    return { totals:totals, infs:infs };
  }

  function pctVsRef(values) {
    var refIdx = INFRA_ORDER.indexOf(infraCompRef);
    var refVal = values[refIdx];
    return values.map(function(v, i) {
      if (i === refIdx) return null;
      if (!refVal) return null;
      return ((v - refVal) / refVal) * 100;
    });
  }

  var infraComparisonChart = new Chart(document.getElementById('infraComparisonChart'), {
    type:'bar',
    data:{
      labels: INFRA_ORDER.map(function(m){ return INFRA_LABELS[m]; }),
      datasets:[
        { label:'Total process (Wh)', data:[], backgroundColor:'#036aa1', borderRadius:4, barPercentage:0.7, categoryPercentage:0.6 },
        { label:'Inference (Wh)',     data:[], backgroundColor:'#A0DCE8', borderRadius:4, barPercentage:0.7, categoryPercentage:0.6 }
      ]
    },
    options:{
      responsive:true, maintainAspectRatio:false,
      animation:{ duration:500, easing:'easeInOutQuart' },
      layout:{ padding:{ top:24 } },
      plugins:{
        legend:{ display:false },
        tooltip:{ callbacks:{ label:function(ctx){ return ' '+ctx.dataset.label+': '+ctx.parsed.y.toFixed(1)+' Wh'; } } }
      },
      scales:{
        x:{ grid:{color:'rgba(128,128,128,0.08)'}, ticks:{color:'#888'} },
        y:{ beginAtZero:true, title:{display:true,text:'Energy (Wh)',color:'#888',font:{size:12}}, grid:{color:'rgba(128,128,128,0.08)'}, ticks:{color:'#888',callback:function(v){ return v+' Wh'; }} }
      }
    },
    plugins:[{
      id:'pctLabels',
      afterDatasetsDraw:function(chart) {
        var ctx = chart.ctx;
        var refIdx = INFRA_ORDER.indexOf(infraCompRef);
        chart.data.datasets.forEach(function(dataset, di) {
          var meta = chart.getDatasetMeta(di);
          var pcts = pctVsRef(dataset.data);
          meta.data.forEach(function(bar, i) {
            ctx.save();
            ctx.font = '11px sans-serif';
            ctx.textAlign = 'center';
            if (i === refIdx) {
              ctx.fillStyle = '#888';
              ctx.fillText('ref', bar.x, bar.y - 8);
            } else if (pcts[i] !== null && !isNaN(pcts[i])) {
              ctx.fillStyle = pcts[i] >= 0 ? '#c7370b' : '#166534';
              var sign = pcts[i] >= 0 ? '+' : '';
              ctx.fillText(sign+pcts[i].toFixed(0)+'%', bar.x, bar.y - 8);
            }
            ctx.restore();
          });
        });
      }
    }]
  });


  function buildInfraCompLegend() {
    var legend = document.getElementById('infraCompLegend');
    if (!legend) return;
    legend.innerHTML =
      '<span style="display:flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;"><span style="width:12px;height:12px;border-radius:3px;background:#036aa1;display:inline-block;"></span>Total process</span>'
      + '<span style="display:flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;"><span style="width:12px;height:12px;border-radius:3px;background:#A0DCE8;display:inline-block;"></span>Inference only</span>';
  }

  function refreshInfraComparisonChart() {
    var d = getInfraCompData();
    infraComparisonChart.data.datasets[0].data = d.totals;
    infraComparisonChart.data.datasets[1].data = d.infs;
    infraComparisonChart.update();
  }

  function populateInfraCompModelSelect() {
    var sel = document.getElementById('infraCompModelSelect');
    if (!sel) return;
    sel.innerHTML = '';
    MODEL_NAMES.forEach(function(name, i) {
      var opt = document.createElement('option');
      opt.value = i;
      opt.textContent = name;
      if (i === infraCompModelIndex) opt.selected = true;
      sel.appendChild(opt);
    });
  }

  window.updateInfraComparisonModel = function(idx) {
    infraCompModelIndex = parseInt(idx, 10);
    refreshInfraComparisonChart();
  };

  window.setInfraComparisonRef = function(m) {
    infraCompRef = m;
    document.getElementById('btn-ref-lir').classList.toggle('active', m==='A');
    document.getElementById('btn-ref-edito').classList.toggle('active', m==='B');
    document.getElementById('btn-ref-eumetsat').classList.toggle('active', m==='C');
    refreshInfraComparisonChart();
  };

  populateInfraCompModelSelect();
  buildInfraCompLegend();
  refreshInfraComparisonChart();

  



  // ── Refresh all charts ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
  function refreshCharts() {
    var m = currentMachine;
    // line
    lineChart.data.datasets = buildLineDatasets(m);
    lineChart.update();
    buildLegend(m);
    // breakdown
    updateBreakdownBars(m);
    // inference bar
    inferenceChart.data.labels = filteredLabels();
    inferenceChart.data.datasets[0].data = activeIndices().map(function(i){ return ALL_INFERENCE[m][i]; });
    inferenceChart.update();
    // duration bar
    durationChart.data.labels = filteredLabels();
    durationChart.data.datasets[0].data = activeIndices().map(function(i){ return ALL_DURATION_TOTAL[m][i]; });
    durationChart.data.datasets[1].data = activeIndices().map(function(i){ return ALL_DURATION_INFERENCE[m][i]; });
    durationChart.update();
    // params
    nbParamsChart.data.labels = filteredLabels();
    nbParamsChart.data.datasets[0].data = activeIndices().map(function(i){ return ALL_NB_PARAMS[m][i]; });
    nbParamsChart.data.datasets[0].backgroundColor = activeIndices().map(function(i){ return MODEL_COLORS[i]; });
    nbParamsChart.update();
    // ope
    nbOpeChart.data.labels = filteredLabels();
    nbOpeChart.data.datasets[0].data = activeIndices().map(function(i){ return ALL_NB_OPE[m][i]; });
    nbOpeChart.data.datasets[0].backgroundColor = activeIndices().map(function(i){ return MODEL_COLORS[i]; });
    nbOpeChart.update();
    // correlation
    var corrResult = buildCorrelationDatasets(m);
    correlationChart.data.datasets = corrResult.datasets;
    correlationChart.update();
    // correlation duration vs ops
    var corrDurationOps = buildGenericCorrelationDatasets(m, ALL_DURATION_TOTAL, ALL_ENERGY_TOTAL);
    correlationDurationOpsChart.data.datasets = corrDurationOps.datasets;
    correlationDurationOpsChart.update();
    // correlation duration vs energy
    var corrDurationEnergy = buildGenericCorrelationDatasets(m, ALL_DURATION_INFERENCE, ALL_ENERGY_INFERENCE);
    correlationDurationEnergyChart.data.datasets = corrDurationEnergy.datasets;
    correlationDurationEnergyChart.update();
  }

  // ── Global controls ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  window.switchAll = function(m) {
    currentMachine = m;
    document.getElementById('btn-lir').classList.toggle('active', m==='A');
    document.getElementById('btn-edito').classList.toggle('active', m==='B');
    document.getElementById('btn-eumetsat').classList.toggle('active', m==='C');
    refreshCharts();
  };

  window.toggleModel = function(name) {
    activeModels[name] = !activeModels[name];
    var chk = document.getElementById('chk-'+name);
    if (chk) chk.classList.toggle('checked', activeModels[name]);
    refreshCharts();
  };

  // ── Stacked bars (individual tab) ────────────────────────────────────────
  function makeStackedBar(barId, legendId, data) {
    var bar = document.getElementById(barId);
    var legend = document.getElementById(legendId);
    if (!bar) return;
    bar.innerHTML = ''; legend.innerHTML = '';
    var total = data.values.reduce(function(a,b){ return a+b; },0);
    data.labels.forEach(function(label, i) {
      var pct = (data.values[i]/total)*100;
      var seg = document.createElement('div');
      seg.title = label+': '+data.values[i]+' ('+pct.toFixed(1)+'%)';
      seg.style.cssText = 'width:'+pct+'%;background:'+data.colors[i]+';height:100%;transition:opacity .2s;cursor:default;';
      seg.onmouseenter = function(){ this.style.opacity='0.75'; };
      seg.onmouseleave = function(){ this.style.opacity='1'; };
      bar.appendChild(seg);
      legend.innerHTML += '<span style="display:flex;align-items:center;gap:5px;">'
        +'<span style="width:10px;height:10px;border-radius:2px;background:'+data.colors[i]+';flex-shrink:0;"></span>'
        +label+' — '+pct.toFixed(1)+'%</span>';
    });
  }

  var STAGE_COLORS = ["#A0DCE8","#036aa1","#1C3A6E"];
  var STAGE_LABELS = ["PRE-INFERENCE","INFERENCE","POST-INFERENCE"];

  function initStackedBars() {
    makeStackedBar('stacked-bar-glonet',       'bar-legend-glonet',       { labels:STAGE_LABELS, values:[40.8,37.2,22.0],          colors:STAGE_COLORS });
    makeStackedBar('stacked-bar-glonet_part2', 'bar-legend-glonet_part2', { labels:STAGE_LABELS, values:[57.2,18.5,24.3],            colors:STAGE_COLORS });
    makeStackedBar('stacked-bar-wenhai',       'bar-legend-wenhai',       { labels:STAGE_LABELS, values:[20.68,66.1,13.2],      colors:STAGE_COLORS });
    makeStackedBar('stacked-bar-wenhai_part2', 'bar-legend-wenhai_part2', { labels:STAGE_LABELS, values:[31.8,49.1,19.1],           colors:STAGE_COLORS });
    makeStackedBar('stacked-bar-xihe',         'bar-legend-xihe',         { labels:STAGE_LABELS, values:[24.0,56.0,20.0],        colors:STAGE_COLORS });
    makeStackedBar('stacked-bar-xihe_part2',   'bar-legend-xihe_part2',   { labels:STAGE_LABELS, values:[33.6,30.8,36.6],           colors:STAGE_COLORS });
    makeStackedBar('stacked-bar-langya',       'bar-legend-langya',       { labels:STAGE_LABELS, values:[39.39,19.2,36.7],          colors:STAGE_COLORS });
    makeStackedBar('stacked-bar-langya_part2', 'bar-legend-langya_part2', { labels:STAGE_LABELS, values:[41,11.7,36.6],          colors:STAGE_COLORS });
    makeStackedBar('stacked-bar-glonet2',       'bar-legend-glonet2',       { labels:STAGE_LABELS, values:[38.9,47.2,13.9],          colors:STAGE_COLORS });
    makeStackedBar('stacked-bar-glonet2_part2', 'bar-legend-glonet2_part2', { labels:STAGE_LABELS, values:[71.7,22.0,6.3],          colors:STAGE_COLORS });
    makeStackedBar('stacked-bar-glonet22',       'bar-legend-glonet22',       { labels:STAGE_LABELS, values:[38.9,47.2,13.9],          colors:STAGE_COLORS });
    makeStackedBar('stacked-bar-glonet2_part22', 'bar-legend-glonet2_part22', { labels:STAGE_LABELS, values:[71.7,22.0,6.3],          colors:STAGE_COLORS });
  }

  window._stackedBarsReady = initStackedBars;
  setTimeout(initStackedBars, 100);

  // ── Init comparison tab charts ───────────────────────────────────────────
  buildBreakdownBars();
  setTimeout(function(){ updateBreakdownBars('B'); }, 50);
  buildLegend('B');
  buildDurationLegend();

});
